text:
Maria: morning handoff — quick recap of last 6h and current status
Maria: overnight we saw a KV-cache eviction storm after the autoscaler tuned down replicas for embeddings; that caused short-lived 503/502s for a slice of traffic. paging fired ~02:14 and we had multiple customer-facing errors for ~12m. :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Pager alert: 3 distinct pages triggered between 02:14-02:28 for service=kv-cache evictions high, severity=SEV2
Maria: what we did: rolled back the recent routing change (route weight revert), temporarily pinned model-variant small-quant on the most impacted pool, and forced a warm-up of prefix cache. This cut error rate to near zero by 02:30.
Alex: saw the same in metrics — p95 token latency spiked to 1.8s briefly, error rate peaked ~4.2% per minute on region-us-west-2 (embedding path).
Sam: confirmed no long-tail customer retries, most hits were within internal batch window. Some retry storms because clients retried aggressively.
Jin: FYI I left a small mitigation: disabled autoscaler downscale-to-zero for embedding-pool-3 for next 12h. We should revisit scaling policy.
Maria: coverage note — primary for morning watch is Alex, secondary is Sam. I'm passing primary to Alex now. I'm available for escalation until 10:30.
Alex: taking primary. confirmed runbook steps executed. leaving comment in incident doc.
Sam: I'll cover secondary and watch customer slack channels; ping me if the rollback needs to be permanent.
Jin: flagged possible root cause: autoscaler growth heuristic + sparse warm cache after weight revert. I'll add extra metrics to the dash (cache-hit-rate by prefix length).
Maria: next steps / action items:
- Alex: monitor p99/p95 for next 3h and watch for eviction recurrence. if error rate >0.5%/5m rollback to the pinned-variant permanently and call an emergency change.
- Sam: coordinate with solutions-eng to identify any clients doing exponential retries; ask them to backoff.
- Jin: create a short follow-up PR to change autoscaler downscale window from 5m -> 20m for embedding pools; include test plan.
- Maria: write post-incident note, add customer impact summary and timeline; target draft by EOD.

Alex: a couple of runbook pointers I used earlier:
- runbook: kv-cache evictions -> check eviction_rate, node_memory_pressure, batcher_queue_length
- commands I ran:
```
# quick checks
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=embedding-pool-3
promtool query instant "sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (pool)"
```
Alex: saved searches: logs query: `status:5xx AND route:embedding AND env:prod`

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction ; Playbook steps summarized: 1) identify pool, 2) pin model variant, 3) warm prefix cache, 4) scale up minimum replicas, 5) notify customers if >10min impact

oncall-bot: Reminder: schedule a post-incident retro if impact >5m to customers.

Maria: coverage gaps to note: no one from infra-auto was on call last night; we should consider a rotation change if autoscaler churn continues. Also alert thresholds need a quick review — eviction_rate alerted at 30m window which was too slow for this burst.
Alex: agreed — suggest a new short-window alert (1m) for eviction spikes + synthetic check that hits embeddings route every 30s during off-peak.
Sam: leaving a TODO in the ops backlog: add client-side backoff guidance to the developer-portal.
Jin: will start the autoscaler PR today and share link here when draft is up.
Maria: final status: incident resolved, no open pages, customer impact limited and mitigated; primary handoff to Alex (watch until 11:00), secondary Sam. Please ack once you have coverage. :thumbsup:
Alex: ack — primary on call.
Sam: ack — secondary on call.
Jin: ack — will post PR link when ready.
Maria: thanks team — I'll drop the incident stub in #postmortems and tag affected customers for communication.
